searchText: Is there a great great specification of Snap Sync? Nice to haves: * comparing it with other forms of snapshot syncing, like the old warp sync, fast sync, or other L1s' snapshot protocols? * how does verkle impact it? Flagging this new paper by Lei @ MegaETH et al which can be used for more efficient snapshot sync protocols: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.02668.pdf. cc <@&688090867927482525> <@&652918665943056397> as snap syncooors The official spec is here: https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/caps/snap.md It has a comparison with fast sync and warp sync, and a rationale The algorithm you linked is interesting, but as noted in paper, it's an improvement for the healing phase only The healing part of snap sync is basically the fast sync protocol from before It's also an interesting question how they handle pivot block movement. It's not explained very well in the paper, would be nice to have the code... Another important thing about Rateless IBLT from the paper is that it requires storing the 'coded symbols'. At the size of Ethereum state, this can be prohibitive. With snap sync as it is, the node only needs to store the actual state in its native form. devp2p/caps/snap.md at master · ethereum... excerpts.content:
Is there a great great specification of Snap Sync?

Nice to haves:
* comparing it with other forms of snapshot syncing, like the old warp sync, fast sync, or other L1s' snapshot protocols? 
* how does verkle impact it?

Flagging this new paper by Lei @ MegaETH et al which can be used for more efficient snapshot sync protocols: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.02668.pdf.

cc <@&688090867927482525> <@&652918665943056397> as snap syncooors

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: It has a comparison with fast sync and warp sync, and a rationale

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The algorithm you linked is interesting, but as noted in paper, it's an improvement for the healing phase only

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: The healing part of snap sync is basically the fast sync protocol from before

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: It's also an interesting question how they handle pivot block movement. It's not explained very well in the paper, would be nice to have the code...

excerpts.author: .fjl
excerpts.content: Another important thing about Rateless IBLT from the paper is that it requires storing the 'coded symbols'. At the size of Ethereum state, this can be prohibitive. With snap sync as it is, the node only needs to store the actual state in its native form.
